Single Responsibility — The draft focuses on one concern: separating agent-dependent tests from the default test path for speed and workflow clarity.; Unambiguous Requirements — At least one requirement uses non-verifiable wording ("approximately 80s instead of 190s") without strict acceptance criteria.; Complete Context — Requirements consistently include trigger conditions (When) and expected outcomes (shall).; No Hardcoded Secrets — No secrets (keys/tokens/passwords) are present; this draft is about test routing and CLI behavior.; Prioritize Requirements — The draft explicitly provides priority order and P1/P2/P3 labels across more than three requirements.; Impact on Existing Features — It explicitly lists impacted existing behaviors and also states unaffected areas.; Present Recommendations with Reasoning — Q&A provides recommendations, but rationale is not consistently grounded in docs/, guardrails, or existing code patterns as required.; Explore Before Asking — Whether docs/code exploration occurred before asking cannot be confirmed from the draft text alone.; Proactively Raise Related Implications — It proactively raises related implications, especially CI parity and required `npm run test:all` migration outside current scope.; Confirm Brainstorm vs. Decision Before Critiquing — No user idea is being critiqued as a final decision in this draft context.; Capture Digressions in draft.md — No evident digression thread requiring capture in `draft.md` is present.; Draft Stays at Requirements Level — The draft stays mostly at requirements/spec level and avoids function-level implementation design.; Backward-Compatible CLI Interface — It identifies changed `npm test` behavior and provides migration guidance to `npm run test:all`.

Single Responsibility — Draft is focused on one concern: separating real AI-agent tests from the default test path.; Unambiguous Requirements — Requirements are phrased with concrete triggers and verifiable outcomes (exclude/run/reject/update docs).; Complete Context — Each listed requirement includes a When condition and a shall behavior.; No Hardcoded Secrets — No source code or secret literals are included in this requirements draft.; Prioritize Requirements — More than three requirements are present and explicitly prioritized with P1/P2 and priority order.; Impact on Existing Features — Impacts are explicitly listed for both affected and unaffected existing features.; Present Recommendations with Reasoning — Each Q&A item leads with a recommended answer and includes concise rationale from docs, guardrails, issue evidence, or code patterns.; Explore Before Asking — The draft uses self-Q&A backed by existing issue/profile/docs context instead of deferring answerable questions to the user.; Proactively Raise Related Implications — It proactively raises CI/default-command and selector-compatibility implications.; Confirm Brainstorm vs. Decision Before Critiquing — No critique of user-proposed decisions is performed; the draft records proposed decisions directly.; Capture Digressions in draft.md — No digressions are evident that required separate capture.; Draft Stays at Requirements Level — Content stays at requirements/scope level without function-level implementation design.; Backward-Compatible CLI Interface — Existing default test behavior is changed, but migration is only partially noted; no concrete migration plan is specified for impacted callers/CI.
